title: Charge transport in two-dimensional conductors with hybrid three-component plasma
authors: A. D. Levin, V. A. Chitta, Z. D. Kvon, N. N. Mikhailov, G. M. Gusev
abstract: Electron--hole plasma in two-dimensional systems has mainly been studied in two limiting cases: degenerate semimetals with parabolic bands and nondegenerate symmetric Dirac systems such as graphene. Here we investigate a different regime realized in a gapless HgTe quantum well: a multicomponent plasma where massless Dirac carriers coexist with thermally activated heavy holes from lateral valence-band valleys. Near charge neutrality, the resistance increases approximately as $T^2$, in sharp contrast to the nearly temperature-independent resistivity expected for a symmetric Dirac plasma. We show that once heavy holes are populated, charge neutrality pins the chemical potential above the Dirac point, leaving the Dirac electrons moderately degenerate while the heavy holes remain nondegenerate and obey Boltzmann statistics. The light electrons therefore scatter almost elastically from the heavy holes, allowing a relaxation-time treatment of interparticle transport. Using carrier densities from self-consistent band-structure calculations, we reproduce the data with a short-range electron--hole interaction in the weakly disordered limit, for which the conductivity scales as $T^{-2}$ and the excess resistivity is proportional to the heavy-hole density. In contrast, an unscreened Coulomb interaction would give a temperature-independent conductivity. The extracted interaction amplitude is of the expected Coulomb scale. These results establish near-critical HgTe quantum wells as a platform for interaction-driven transport in multicomponent systems combining degenerate massless and nondegenerate massive carriers.
summary: This work investigates charge transport in a unique three-component plasma realized in HgTe quantum wells, combining massless Dirac electrons with thermally activated heavy holes. By analyzing the temperature dependence of resistivity, the authors demonstrate that the observed quadratic increase selects for a short-range electron-heavy-hole interaction mechanism. This establishes the material as a key platform for studying interaction-driven transport in mixed-carrier quantum systems.
main_problem: Investigating charge transport in a hybrid three-component plasma system involving massless Dirac carriers and thermally activated heavy holes.
main_result: The observed temperature-dependent resistivity ($ho \propto T^2$) is attributed to a short-range electron-heavy-hole interaction, contrasting with predictions from unscreened Coulomb interactions.
method: The analysis uses a non-perturbative, momentum-relaxation-time description of interparticle transport, fitting measured resistivity data to theoretical scaling laws.
model_or_system: The system is modeled using a gapless HgTe quantum well hosting three components: degenerate massless Dirac electrons, Dirac holes, and non-degenerate heavy holes. The charge neutrality condition must be satisfied self-consistently.
key_observables: Resistivity ($ho$) vs. Temperature ($T$), excess resistivity ($\Deltaho$), and carrier densities ($n_d, p_d, p_{HH}$).
important_parameters: Temperature range ($T \gtrsim 10$ K), heavy-hole density ($p_{HH}$), and the interaction amplitude ($U_0 \approx 90 	ext{ eV nm}^2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the scattering is quasi-elastic and treats the system in the weakly disordered limit, using a minimal effective reference model for the gapless spectrum.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectrum, the Density of States (DOS) for the three components, and the temperature evolution of the carrier densities, showing the crossover between different plasma regimes.
paper_structure: The paper develops the physics by first establishing the unique three-component nature of the plasma, then using self-consistent calculations to track carrier populations with temperature, and finally applying kinetic theory to link the observed temperature dependence of resistivity to the specific interaction channel (short-range vs. Coulomb).
why_interesting: The study provides a concrete platform for observing interaction-driven transport in a hybrid system combining different types of quantum statistics (degenerate massless vs. non-degenerate massive), which is relevant for understanding strongly correlated behavior in low-dimensional materials.
